question.worked_solution:
First, we convert the given probability into a cumulative probability using the complement:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & =1-P(X>2) \\  & =1-0.2981 \\  & =0.7019\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & =0.7019 \\ P(Z\le \frac{2-\mu }{5}) & =0.7019 \\ Φ(\frac{2-\mu }{5}) & =0.7019 \\ \frac{2-\mu }{5} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7019)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.53)=0.7019\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7019)=0.53.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2-\mu }{5} & =0.53 \\ 2-\mu  & =2.65 \\ \mu  & =-0.65.\end{aligned}
$$
